questions.title: Maximum Sum of K Consecutive Numbers
questions.description:
Given an array of `n` integers, find the largest possible sum of any `k` consecutive elements.

### Input
- Line 1: two space-separated integers `n` and `k` (the array size and window size), with `1 <= k <= n`.
- Line 2: `n` space-separated integers, the array itself (values may be negative).

### Output
Print a single integer: the maximum sum achievable by adding up `k` consecutive elements of the array.

### Example
Input:
```
8 3
2 1 5 1 3 2 8 1
```
Output:
```
13
```
Explanation: the windows of size 3 are `[2,1,5]`, `[1,5,1]`, `[5,1,3]`, `[1,3,2]`, `[3,2,8]`, `[2,8,1]`, with sums `8, 7, 9, 6, 13, 11`. The largest is `13`, from `[3,2,8]`.

### Note
A simple approach is to try every window and sum its `k` elements from scratch (this will pass). If you finish early, think about how to reuse the previous window's sum instead of re-adding all `k` elements each time (a sliding window).

testCases.description: k = n, whole array with all negatives
array with mixed negative and positive values
